design_note: Replaces an abstract scheduler cycle with three concrete batch rosters. Completed work leaves while a longer request remains, so changing membership becomes visible without a throughput claim.

source.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
source.publisher: Gyeong-In Yu and coauthors; USENIX OSDI 2022
source.concept: Scheduling generation at iteration boundaries allows the active batch membership to change before every request in the earlier batch finishes.
source.scope: Original three-request roster; capacity, admission and preprocessing are simplified. No ORCA performance result or figure is reproduced.

lesson.title: A finished request gives up its place
lesson.intro: A constructed decoder has two request slots. A and B are active; C is eligible and prepared to enter. B needs two more steps and A needs four. Track only membership.

frames.title: Boundary 0
frames.event: A and B continue; C waits

frames.title: Boundary 2
frames.event: B finishes; C takes free slot

data.invariant: A long request does not force a finished request to keep its slot.

read: At boundary 2, A is still running but B has left.
C enters the available slot before A finishes.
At boundary 4, C has completed two of its three required steps.
lesson.question: Must C wait until boundary 4 solely because A and B entered the earlier batch together?
lesson.answer: No. This scheduler can admit prepared C at boundary 2 when B finishes. C then completes at boundary 5 under the toy one-step-per-iteration assumption. Real admission also depends on memory, prefill, scheduling policy and fairness; two depicted slots do not establish device capacity or a speedup guarantee.
lesson.takeaway: Continuous batching changes the active roster as requests become ready or finish.
lesson.assumption: Constructed two-slot scheduler; each active request advances one step per iteration. C is prefilled; memory, prefill scheduling and timing are omitted.
